text:
Riley (People Ops): Heads-up everyone — we just published an update to our Global Workation & PTO Sync guidance. Short version: if you plan to work from another country for 7+ consecutive calendar days, you now need to submit a Workation Notice at least 14 days in advance and sync PTO/leave with your manager. Full doc: <https://intranet.redwood/people/workation-policy|Workation & PTO sync> :sparkles:

Riley (People Ops): Why the change? We've had a few cases where tax, payroll, or local labor rules were triggered because people were remote from different countries for extended stretches. This update helps us avoid surprise payroll/tax impacts and ensures compliance while keeping workation options open.

Jamie: Quick Q — does this apply if I'm visiting family for 10 days but plan to take 5 PTO + 5 working days?

Riley (People Ops): Yes — the 7+ day rule is about your physical location, regardless of PTO mix. If you're over 7 consecutive days in a different country, submit the Notice. If you take PTO for the whole period you still submit so we can track payroll/tax windows.

Aisha: Does manager approval mean I need HR to sign off too?

Riley (People Ops): Manager approval is required to ensure coverage. For certain countries the policy flags the trip for People Ops review for legal/tax sign-off — you'll see that in the Workation Notice flow. If flagged, People Ops will follow up within 3 business days.

Marco: Are there changes to expense/reimbursement while on workation?

Riley (People Ops): Not major changes. Per-diem/meal caps remain the same. Important: digitize and attach receipts to Expensify within 10 business days. TravelBot will auto-remind once the Notice is created.

TravelBot: Reminder scheduled — submit receipts within 10 business days after travel. Link: <https://tools.redwood/expensify|Expensify> :robot_face:

Samir: Any blackout windows or region restrictions we should know about?

Riley (People Ops): No global blackout, but there are a handful of countries where working remotely triggers local registration or has security concerns. Those are listed in the policy annex. If you're planning a trip to one of those countries, People Ops will require a short risk assessment and may decline workation depending on legal/operational constraints.

Lindsey: How does this affect PTO accrual/usage when crossing payroll months? I have a long trip spanning month end.

Riley (People Ops): Accrual is unchanged — you'll accrue in your home payroll period as usual. If you're on a long trip and intend to take unpaid time or use local statutory leave, reach out to payroll@redwood and cc your manager; we'll advise for your specific case.

Jamie: What about health insurance / coverage while abroad?

Riley (People Ops): Short stays are usually covered; extended stays may not be. Check the benefits FAQ linked from the policy header. For anything >30 days, open a ticket with Benefits (benefits@redwood) before you travel.

Aisha: Is there a template for manager notes when approving?

Riley (People Ops): Yep — the Notice workflow includes an optional manager note field. Suggested items: overlap with sprints, backup contacts, expected timezone overlap.

Marco: If People Ops flags my Notice, is there an appeal/alternative process?

Riley (People Ops): We'll work with you and your manager to find alternatives (split travel, adjust dates, or take PTO). Appeals go to people-ops@redwood with manager endorsement.

Samir: Awesome — thanks for clarifying. small ask: can we get a one-page cheat sheet?

Riley (People Ops): On it. I'll post a one-pager and a 5-min FAQ clip in #people-ops later today.

Lindsey: Thanks — this helps with planning. :thumbsup:

Riley (People Ops): Final reminders: 1) 14-day Notice for 7+ consecutive days; 2) submit receipts within 10 business days; 3) flagged countries require People Ops review; 4) cc payroll/benefits for edge cases. Link again: <https://intranet.redwood/people/workation-policy|Workation & PTO sync>

Jamie: noted. thanks! :raised_hands:

TravelBot: Automated follow-up will post in 3 days for anyone with pending Notices.
